question: A 70-year-old man presents with oliguria. Examination reveals dry mucous membranes, skin turgor reduced, JVP not visible, heart rate 108 bpm, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg. Which pattern of urinalysis results best supports a pre-renal cause for his AKI?

answers.text: Urine sodium <20 mEq/L, urine osmolality >500 mOsm/kg, no casts

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In pre-renal AKI, the kidney is structurally intact and responding to hypoperfusion by avidly conserving sodium (urine Na <20) and concentrating urine (osmolality >500). The absence of casts reflects intact tubular architecture.

answers.text: Urine sodium >40 mEq/L, urine osmolality <350 mOsm/kg, muddy-brown granular casts

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These findings — high urine sodium, dilute urine, and muddy-brown casts — indicate established ATN (intrinsic AKI). Damaged tubules cannot conserve sodium or concentrate urine.

answers.text: Urine sodium >40 mEq/L, urine osmolality >500 mOsm/kg, RBC casts

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. RBC casts indicate glomerulonephritis (intrinsic AKI, glomerular cause). The high osmolality is inconsistent with the damaged concentrating ability expected in established intrinsic AKI.

answers.text: Urine sodium 25 mEq/L, urine osmolality 280 mOsm/kg, WBC casts

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. WBC casts suggest acute interstitial nephritis (intrinsic AKI). The near-isoosmotic urine indicates tubular dysfunction inconsistent with pre-renal AKI.

overallFeedback.feedback: In pre-renal AKI, intact tubules avidly conserve sodium (urine Na <20) and concentrate urine (osmolality >500), with no casts. Contrast with ATN (urine Na >40, low osmolality, muddy-brown casts).
Correct. Pre-renal AKI: urine Na <20, osmolality >500, no casts — intact tubules concentrating avidly. ATN: urine Na >40, osmolality <350, muddy-brown casts. FENa <1% also supports pre-renal.
